_README: Industry events / semiconductor conferences that can move watchlist names via product announcements, roadmap disclosures, or competitive read-through. The morning routine (CLAUDE.md) refreshes dates and 'watch' notes via web search each run and adds newly-announced events. 'tickers' = watchlist symbols with direct or read-through exposure. 'partners' = KEY PRIVATE/NON-WATCHLIST COMPANIES whose appearances matter because a holding depends on them (e.g. Ayar Labs is Sivers' flagship CPO customer; Lightmatter is the CPO peer benchmark). ADDED 2026-08-07 after OCP APAC was missed: relevance must be checked against BOTH tickers and partners, and MAJOR EVENT SERIES HAVE REGIONAL EDITIONS (OCP runs Global + APAC + EMEA; SEMICON runs West/Taiwan/Europe/Korea) — enumerate every edition, not just the flagship. 'confidence': confirmed (dates verified) | approx (typical timing, verify) | rumored. Dates ISO YYYY-MM-DD, event-local. Not investment advice.

events.name: Marvell Technology Investor Day 2026
events.location: New York City (in-person by invitation; live webcast)
events.watch: **ADDED 2026-08-18 (morning run) — a real calendar gap: a watchlist company has a confirmed, dated, WEBCAST management event and this calendar did not carry it.** **Marvell announced on 2026-08-03, in the same release that set its Q2 FY2027 earnings call, that it will hold an Investor Day on the morning of Tue Oct 6, 2026 in New York City, with Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy and the senior leadership team presenting.** In-person attendance is by invitation only, but **the event is webcast live via the Events section of investor.marvell.com** — which is what separates this from the broker conferences elsewhere on this calendar: it is a company-controlled disclosure venue with a public feed, not a 1x1 program. It sat unlogged for fifteen days. **Why it matters for this book specifically: an investor day is where multi-year financial targets and segment models get set, and MRVL is the one watchlist name whose thesis turns on a disclosure of exactly that kind.** The MRVL falsifiers are "loss/insourcing of a flagship custom program", "CPO disintermediates pluggable DSPs faster than Marvell adapts", and a shift in data-center guide language — all three are TAM-and-roadmap claims that an investor day either substantiates with a model or conspicuously does not. **Sequencing is the other reason to carry it: the Q2 FY2027 print lands Thu Aug 27 at 1:45pm PT, five and a half weeks BEFORE this event**, so the quarter sets the near-term facts and the investor day sets the multi-year frame on top of them. Note the tape context this is being scheduled into: **UBS cut its MRVL target 340 → 300 on 2026-08-17**, and the name has run 74 → 316 and back inside six months. **Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier yet — it is a scheduled opportunity for one to be adjudicated.** 49 days out; outside the 30-day window, carried so it is not missed again. **Re-verified 2026-09-23 run — 13 days out, now inside the 14-day window.** Date, venue and format re-confirmed at source (Marvell IR): **morning of Tue Oct 6, 2026, New York City, Chairman/CEO Matt Murphy plus the senior leadership team, in-person by invitation, webcast live via the Events section of investor.marvell.com with a replay after.** No session-level agenda is published at source as of this pass. **Sharpening this pass, and label it honestly: third-party previews (not Marvell) frame the event as the venue for the long-term custom-silicon trajectory, scale-up optics and a fiscal-2029 revenue outlook. Marvell itself has published no topic list, so treat those three as EXPECTATION, not scheduled content.** If a multi-year model does appear, it is the disclosure that bears on the recorded falsifiers 'loss/insourcing of a flagship custom program' and 'CPO disintermediates pluggable DSPs faster than Marvell adapts' — an investor day either substantiates a segment model or conspicuously does not. Cross-read: it lands 12 days after ECOC closes, so the CPO/NPO vendor evidence logged on the ECOC entry this week (Coherent PhotonLink spanning CPO+NPO, Lumentum's 8-wavelength ELSFP) is the competitive backdrop Marvell will be presenting a DSP/optics roadmap against. Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier yet. **Re-verified 2026-09-25 run — 11 days out.** Date, venue, format unchanged at source (morning of Tue Oct 6, 2026, New York City, CEO Matt Murphy plus senior leadership, in-person by invitation, live webcast via investor.marvell.com with replay). **No session-level agenda published at source as of this pass.** Sharpening this pass, labelled by source: **Marvell's own framing in the announcement is 'showcasing growth drivers and long-term strategy for enabling the continued expansion of AI infrastructure'**, with the company having pointed to broad-based data-center strength and **a significant acceleration in the custom business beginning in H2 fiscal 2027** — that acceleration claim is the one management-sourced number this event can either model out or walk back, and it sits directly on the 'loss/insourcing of a flagship custom program' falsifier. **Third-party, NOT Marvell: sell-side previews expect a positive event driven by scale-up connectivity and the Google partnership, and expect a multi-year TAM framework like prior investor days; Morgan Stanley raised its target ahead of the date. Treat all of that as expectation-setting, not disclosure.** Calibrate: an investor day is a scheduled opportunity for a falsifier to be adjudicated — nothing is adjudicated until Marvell presents.

events.name: OCP Global Summit 2026 (Open Compute Project)
events.watch: Hyperscaler datacenter standards — rack power/cooling, networking fabrics, custom silicon, optics adoption. Meta is a core OCP driver (capex read-through); networking/optics read-through for AVGO & MRVL; datacenter-infrastructure read-through for WULF's HPC-conversion thesis.

events.name: SEMICON West 2026
events.watch: Dates confirmed 2026-07-22 via the official SEMI organizer site (Pre-Show Day Mon Oct 12, show floor Oct 13-15). Fab-equipment/WFE industry event, almost exactly overlapping the existing OCP Global Summit (Oct 12-15, San Jose) — same catalyst week. Relevant to TSM (leading-edge capacity/pricing commentary) and GFS (specialty-foundry, onshoring/CHIPS Act positioning).

events.name: GlobalFoundries Technology Summit (GTS) 2026 — Europe
events.watch: **ADDED 2026-09-03 (promoted from the GTS North America entry, whose Sep 2 date has now passed and which was removed this run).** GF's flagship customer/partner technology summit runs as a regional series; per the README's regional-edition rule the remaining 2026 editions each get their own entry as they come inside the 30-day window. **Dates re-verified this run against GF's own GTS page: Shanghai Sep 22, Hsinchu Sep 24, Munich Oct 15.** Format is GF and industry-leader keynotes plus deep dives into GF's differentiated process platforms (RF-SOI, silicon photonics, FD-SOI, automotive/power) and customer/ecosystem results. **Why it matters for GFS: this is where the specialty-foundry case acquires roadmap and design-win evidence bearing on the drivers "specialty mix defends pricing vs commodity nodes" and "silicon photonics becomes a real revenue line as CPO scales" — it does NOT bear on the pricing-war or utilisation falsifiers.** Secondary read: GF is named in the SIVE thesis as an ecosystem partner (GlobalFoundries reference designs for hyperscalers incl. AMD), so any silicon-photonics platform announcement is a read-through into the CPO chain. **Calibrate honestly: a customer/partner technology event, not an investor day — expect platform and partnership announcements, not guidance, and no session-level agenda is published at source for these editions as of this pass. Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier.** Final edition of the 2026 series. **Note the Oct 15 collision: OCP Global Summit (Oct 12-15) and SEMICON West (Oct 13-15) both overlap it, so GF news that day competes for attention with two larger venues.** 42 days out — outside the 30-day window, carried as a placeholder so the series is not lost.

events.name: IEDM 2026 (72nd IEEE International Electron Devices Meeting)
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: premier device-physics/process-tech conference, theme 'Devices at the Heart of the Intelligence Revolution.' Expect next-node transistor (GAA/CFET) and advanced-packaging/substrate papers directly relevant to Soitec's SOI/substrate roadmap plus TSM/INTC/GFS process roadmaps. Detailed accepted-paper program not yet released; dates flagged 'subject to change' by some listings — verify closer to the event.

events.name: CES 2027
events.watch: Consumer + edge-AI keynotes; NVIDIA typically opens with a roadmap/keynote. Broad AI-infrastructure tone-setter for the year. 60th-anniversary edition.

events.name: OFC 2027 (Optical Fiber Communication Conference & Exposition)
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: the largest global optics show — the semiannual bookend to ECOC for CPO/transceiver/InP-laser roadmap disclosures (1.6T/3.2T transceivers, co-packaged optics), directly feeding the Sivers/Soitec thesis.

events.name: NVIDIA GTC 2027
events.watch: NVIDIA's flagship — next-gen architecture (post-Rubin) roadmap, networking (NVLink/Spectrum), and increasingly CPO/optics partners. The single biggest AI-infra catalyst of the year; read-through across the entire watchlist, especially the optics chain if NVDA advances co-packaged optics.

events.name: OCP EMEA Summit 2027 (Open Compute Project)
events.watch: **ROLLED FORWARD 2026-08-12 (end-of-day run): the 2026 EMEA edition's end date (2026-04-22) had passed, and this entry has been replaced with the confirmed 2027 edition — Apr 6-8, 2027, Hamburg, Germany**, verified against OCP's own summit page. This is the placeholder the 2026 entry was explicitly being kept for, so the series stays fully enumerated (Global + APAC + EMEA) without carrying a dead date. Far out of the alert window; relevance is the same as the other OCP editions — open datacenter hardware, rack power/cooling, networking fabrics and optics adoption, with the photonics chain (Lightmatter as the CPO peer benchmark) the reason this book tracks the series at all.
